title: Fabrication and Use of Dry Macroporous Alginate Scaffolds for Viral Transduction of T Cells
protocol: Prepare a stock solution of 0.4% calcium D gluconate by adding sterile-filtered deionized water to calcium D gluconate in a beaker.
Stir on medium speed until the calcium gluconate has dissolved (~1.5 h).
Sterile-filter the prepared solution.
Store the stock solution at room temperature.
Prepare a solution of 2% (weight per volume) alginate in a screw cap vial or beaker.
Add ultrapure alginate to the vessel.
Add sterile-filtered deionized water to the alginate.
Choose the largest stir bar possible that will not impede mixing and add it to the vessel.
Stir the solution on high speed until the alginate dissolves (~1 h).
Tilt the vessel to dislodge any large clumps on the sides.
Reduce the stirring speed once the alginate has dissolved completely.
Slowly add an equal volume of 0.4% calcium D gluconate to the alginate solution.
Stir vigorously for 15 min.
Tilt the beaker or vial sideways to remove any clumps that may have formed.
Pipette the desired volume of the solution into each well of a 48-well plate or 24-well plate.
Use 300 μl/well for a 48-well plate and 1 ml/well for a 24-well plate.
Cover the plates with lids and freeze overnight at -20 °C.
Remove the lid of the frozen plate and secure it with wipes and rubber bands.
Place the plates in 750 ml to 2,000 ml lyophilizer flasks.
Place the plates on the lyophilizer for 72 h.
After 72 h, remove the plate from the lyophilizer and replace the lid.
Seal the plate and store at 4 °C.
For long term storage, vacuum-seal the plate before storing at 4 °C.
Hydrate the centrifugal filter with 1 ml of 1x phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Discard the PBS.
Concentrate the viral suspension by adding 2 ml of viral suspension and centrifuging it through the centrifugal filter at 1,500 × g for 10 min in a swinging bucket rotor.
Seed activated cells and virus together.
Suspend 1 × 10^6 activated peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) in 50 μl of complete cell culture media.
Add the concentrated viral supernatant (~2 × 10^6 TU, MOI 2) to the cell suspension.
Mix the cell-virus suspension dropwise onto the top of the dry scaffold.
For negative control experiments, use complete cell culture media in place of the concentrated virus and add it to the scaffold.
Incubate the scaffolds in a cell culture incubator at 37 °C for 45-60 min.
Add complete cell culture media supplemented with IL-15 (5 ng/mL) and IL-7 (10 ng/mL) to each well.
Incubate the scaffolds at 37°C for 72 h.
Dilute 0.5 M EDTA to 0.25 M EDTA in 1x PBS.
Remove excess medium from each well and collect into separate 15 mL centrifuge tubes.
Add 0.25 M EDTA to each scaffold (300 µL for 48-well scaffolds or 1 mL for 24-well scaffolds).
Let the plate sit or gently agitate for 3-4 min.
Pipette in and out gently inside the well to fully dissolve the scaffold if necessary.
Add another 200 µL of 0.25 M EDTA if the scaffold does not dissolve in 10 min.
Transfer the solution containing dissolved scaffold to a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Repeat steps for each scaffold.
Wash the cells twice by adding 12 mL PBS to each centrifuge tube and centrifuging at 400 × g for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant and repeat the wash.
The cell pellet is now ready for analysis.
